items.why: The Forever client's MapCanvas (wow-handoff/blizzard-ui Blizzard_MapCanvas/Blizzard_MapCanvas.lua:260-267) creates every pin pool with OnPinReleased, which always calls pin:OnReleased(); RemoveAllPinsByTemplate is ReleaseAll on that pool, so no pooled pin misses OnReleased. items.quote: - **Zone completion**: how much of a zone's Legacy objectives you've done, Guild Wars 2 style. Out of the box it counts areas explored (each is a step of the zone's Explore achievement, toward Explorer) for the character, and dungeons, raids and the zone's other Legacy objectives for your Legacy progress on the account. Flight paths learned and local reputations at Friendly aren't Legacy objectives; tick them under "What counts" to count them too. So can quests, if you have [Questie](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/questie) installed: the zone's quests your character can take, read from Questie's database in game. A zone reaching 100% of what you count gets a toast and a sound, and continent maps show how many of the continent's zones are complete. It shows in the world map's corner, for the zone you're viewing, and in each zone badge's tooltip on continent maps; unticking "On the world map" in the map menu hides both the corner and the continent badges. It can also show in the objective tracker, for the zone you're in (the zone name, a percentage and one row of counts), once you tick that in the map menu. Each can be collapsed, and hovering lists what's left. "What counts" in the same menu adds or leaves out any category, and the percentage and the toast follow.
items.what: one feature bullet of ~230 words across 10 sentences; "What counts" explained twice
items.why: Owner decision (player-facing copy): keep the first two sentences plus where it shows and the 100% toast; the per-category detail already lives in docs/zone-completion.md (linked two sections below), and docs/curseforge.md says the same in ~60 words. The Tracker bullet (line 22, ~140 words) has the same shape.

items.quote:
local function Attach(trackerModule)
	if ForeverTrackerHost then
		ForeverTrackerHost.Attach(trackerModule)
		return
	end
	-- The shared private host is optional; standalone companions stay inert until it loads.
end

local function AttachAll()
	for _, trackerModule in ipairs(modules) do
		Attach(trackerModule)
	end
end

---@param trackerModule LegacyTrackerModule
---@return boolean
local function IsAttached(trackerModule)
	if ForeverTrackerHost then
		return ForeverTrackerHost.IsAttached(trackerModule)
	end
	return false
end
items.what: Attach and IsAttached wrappers guard a missing ForeverTrackerHost for 'standalone companions' that are not in this repo
items.why: TrackerHost.lua loads before Tracker.lua in the TOC and defines the global whenever ObjectiveTrackerFrame exists; Tracker.AddModule returns nil before Attach when the tracker is unavailable, so the nil branch (empty Attach fallthrough, IsAttached returning false) never runs in the shipped addon. Only the lifecycle spec sets the global by hand. Collapsed: call ns.TrackerHost.Attach / IsAttached directly.

Replacing the local Attach/IsAttached wrappers with direct calls passes those cases and an isolated LuaLS check with zero diagnostics, while no shipped loader or in-flight ref omits the host, so the unsupported standalone mode does not justify these forwarding guards.

items.what: Layout is a ~140-line function (164-302) with distinct phases: combat lift above the native slot (166-210), Edit Mode bail-out, module stacking (215-250), off-screen shift (251-280), native viewport height sync (281-301).
items.why: Each phase touches shared upvalues (nativeAnchor, requestedNativeHeight, appliedNativeHeight) but could be a named local (LiftForCombat, StackModules, ClampNativeHeight). The combat and normal paths are what the owner's uncommitted edit is growing, so the split is best done as its own reviewed change after the anchor helper above.
items.reason: The phases form one synchronous layout transaction: the initial anchor determines available height, module updates determine host height, that height changes CENTER/BOTTOM top geometry and off-screen shift, and the final bottom constrains the native viewport while requested/applied heights prevent drift. Combat and Edit Mode short-circuit the same transaction; naming helpers may aid reading but the cited phases do not establish independent responsibilities or a size defect.
